messages.subject: problem in spectro after amplitude filtering
messages.subject_clean: problem in spectro after amplitude filtering
messages.body_plain:
Hi everyone,

I am new to seewave, so this may be obvious:  i have a noisy sound, so i proceeded to an amplitude filtering with afilter(). However, when i increase the amplitude threshold in afilter(), the spectrogram of the resulting sound displays many diagonal lines and is simply unreadable (i have attached the resulting spectro). This does not happen when the threshold is low.

Does anyone has an idea of how to get around this?

Thanks!

Le 11/09/2012 20:10, sandra a écrit :
> Hi everyone,
>
> I am new to seewave, so this may be obvious:  i have a noisy sound, so
> i proceeded to an amplitude filtering with afilter(). However, when i
> increase the amplitude threshold in afilter(), the spectrogram of the
> resulting sound displays many diagonal lines and is simply unreadable
> (i have attached the resulting spectro). This does not happen when the
> threshold is low.
>
> Does anyone has an idea of how to get around this?
>
> Thanks!

Hello,

Well, this is probably because afilter() is a rather stupid function.
afilter() removes everything above the threshold you set up. If the
threshold value is too high you may remove too much sound and give a
square shape to some parts of your signal. That's something the FFT
cannot cope with... and this probably generates this kind of "nice"
spectrogram...

Jerome

messages.subject: setWavPlayer in mac
messages.body_plain:
Hi folks,
Finally I installed seewave in my mac. But now I have a new problem. I´m creating pure tones, but when I try to listen these tones, I can´t.
I have set the wav player in this way (setWavPlayer("~/Applications/Utilities/QuickTime Player 7")), but when I checked the wavplayer with findwavplayer says "No standard wav player known for your system.\n".
How can I set the wav player? any suggestion?
Thanks in advance,
Oscar Laverde.

function ()

{

    command <- switch(R.Version()$os, `linux-gnu` = c("play",

        "playwave"), Win32 = "mplay32 /play", mingw32 = "mplay32 /play",

        darwin8.6.0 = "open -a 'QuickTime Player'", darwin8.6.1 = "open -a 'QuickTime Player'",

        default = NULL)

    if (is.null(command))

        warning("No standard wav player known for your system.\n")

    return(command)

}

<environment: namespace:sound>

messages.subject: Re: [seewave] setWavPlayer in mac
messages.body_plain:
Hi Oscar,

The following works for at least some Macs:

setWavPlayer("afplay")

Regards,
Jesse Ross
